summary: Hand geometry, colours and breathe rhythm are exact, but the port boots into the wrong RadiusMode (full-length wedges, mean brightness 21 vs the original's tiny 4-px blobs at mean 4), three of the four RadiusMode looks differ, and the Speed slider is inverted.
observations: Both sides are completely static at default dials over 240 s (motion 0, zeroMotionFrames = every frame, brightnessTrend steady on both, seed-independent at seed 1 and 7). The pinned wall clock means the hands never tick; there is exactly one regime and no steady-state decay on either side.

Hand geometry is identical. With sliderRadiusMode=1 on both, a --dump of the 16x16 grid gives a mean absolute per-channel difference of 1.0/255 between orig and port, and the contact sheets are visually indistinguishable: hour hand a blue wedge to the upper right, minute a green wedge to the left, second a red wedge to the lower left, all radiating from grid centre. Both sides therefore decode the same pinned clock to the same three angles.

Hand-to-picker mapping matches: setting HourHandColor to yellow recolours the upper-right wedge on both, MinuteHandColor the left wedge, SecondHandColor the lower-left wedge. Given explicit component triples the emitted RGB agrees to 1/255 (orig [255,255,0] vs port [254,255,0]).

DEFAULT LOOK IS WRONG. Original at defaults draws three tiny compact blobs (green 2x2 at grid (2-3,6-7), blue ~5 px around (8-11,5-7), red ~4 px around (1-2,10-12)) on an otherwise black panel, mean brightness 4. Port at defaults draws three full-length filled wedges reaching the panel edge (~15-25 lit px each), mean brightness 21 - a ~5x brighter, structurally different image. Mean abs difference default-vs-default is 16.6/255, the largest of any dial setting tested.

Cause is the RadiusMode default: numerically, the original's untouched output is byte-identical to its sliderRadiusMode=0.25/0.375 render, while the port's untouched output is byte-identical to its sliderRadiusMode=0.875/1 render. The port defaults to the top quarter of the dial; the original defaults to the second quarter.

RadiusMode is a 4-way mode selector on both sides (quarter boundaries), but only the top mode agrees. Original: mode 0 = green wedge from centre plus small blue, red hand absent; mode 1 (its default) = three tiny blobs; mode 2 = medium blobs (~10-13 px each) still short of the edge; mode 3 = full wedges. Port: mode 0 = sparse single-pixel speckle scattered along each hand (~5 px/hand); mode 1 = sparser speckle clustered near centre; mode 2 = small compact blobs near centre (3-5 px/hand); mode 3 = full wedges. Mean abs diff orig-vs-port is 7.6 (mode 0), 6.3-8.0 (modes 1-2), 1.0 (mode 3).

Control surface mismatch: the original exposes rgbPickerHourHandColor / rgbPickerMinuteHandColor / rgbPickerSecondHandColor with kind rgbPicker; the port exposes hsvPickerHourHandColor / hsvPickerMinuteHandColor / hsvPickerSecondHandColor with kind hsvPicker. Different control names and different widget kinds for the same three labels (HourHandColor / MinuteHandColor / SecondHandColor). The six slider controls match exactly in name and kind.

Breathe waveform matches exactly at each side's fast end: at 10 fps over 30 s both peak every 10 frames (1.00 s period) with the same rise/hold/fall shape and the same phase. Only the amplitude differs (see dials).

Strength agrees closely at matched RadiusMode=1 for values up to 0.5 (mean abs diff 1.0 at 0.25, 0.3 at 0.5); above that both saturate into a full-panel noisy wash but with different speckle (diff 22.9 at 0.75, 67.1 at 1.0), which is the blown-out regime on both sides.

dials.name: HourHandColor (orig rgbPickerHourHandColor / port hsvPickerHourHandColor)
dials.origEffect: recolours the upper-right (hour) wedge; explicit RGB triple reproduces exactly
dials.portEffect: same wedge, same emitted colour to 1/255 - but the control is an hsvPicker with a different control name, so the stored value and the UI widget differ

dials.name: MinuteHandColor (orig rgbPickerMinuteHandColor / port hsvPickerMinuteHandColor)
dials.portEffect: same wedge, same colour; control name/kind differ (hsvPicker)

dials.name: SecondHandColor (orig rgbPickerSecondHandColor / port hsvPickerSecondHandColor)
dials.portEffect: same wedge, same colour; control name/kind differ (hsvPicker)

dials.name: sliderRadiusMode
dials.origEffect: 4-way mode switch at quarter boundaries: 0 = green wedge + small blue, no red; 0.25-0.45 = three tiny blobs (the default look); 0.5-0.75 = medium blobs; 0.875-1 = full wedges to the panel edge
dials.portEffect: also a 4-way switch at quarter boundaries, but 0-0.3 = sparse single-pixel speckle, 0.375-0.5 = sparser speckle near centre, 0.625-0.75 = small compact blobs, 0.875-1 = full wedges. Only the top mode matches; the port's default lands in the top mode while the original's default lands in its second

dials.name: sliderSharpness
dials.origEffect: raising it narrows the hands monotonically; at RadiusMode=1 mean brightness falls 85 -> 47 -> 25 -> 16 -> 14 across 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1
dials.portEffect: same direction and same shape, but the hands stay consistently wider: 85 -> 53 -> 32 -> 25 -> 20 over the same sweep (~25-55% more lit area above sharpness 0.25)

dials.name: sliderStrength
dials.origEffect: raising it widens/brightens the hands, 15 -> 30 -> 60 -> 85 (saturated) -> 85 at RadiusMode=1
dials.portEffect: same curve, 10 -> 29 -> 60 -> 76 -> 83; both saturate into a noisy full-panel wash at the top with different speckle

dials.name: sliderBreathe
dials.origEffect: amplitude of a 1 s brightness pulse; mean brightness swing 20-20 / 19-21 / 18-25 / 18-25 / 18-28 across 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 (at Speed=1)
dials.portEffect: same direction and same 1 s period, but roughly 1.8x the amplitude at the top: 21-21 / 20-25 / 19-26 / 19-30 / 19-37 (at Speed=0)

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: breathe rate rises with the dial: Speed=0 is completely frozen (150/150 zero-motion frames over 30 s), 0.5 barely moves (motion avg 0.1), 0.9 motion avg ~1, 1.0 breathes at 1 Hz (motion avg 4.2)
dials.portEffect: INVERTED - Speed=0 breathes fastest (motion avg 7.6, brightness 19-37), 0.1-0.2 motion avg ~1, 0.3-0.5 barely moves, and 1.0 is completely frozen (150/150 zero-motion frames)

dials.name: sliderDistance
dials.origEffect: live in RadiusMode modes 0-1 (at its default mode, 0/0.5/1 changes the blobs from compact clusters to a scattered handful of single pixels, mean 4 -> 3 -> 2); no effect in modes 2-3 (mean 11/11/11 and 22/22/22)
dials.portEffect: no effect at all in the port's default mode or in modes 0-1 (0/0.5/1 give byte-identical frames); in mode 2 it blanks the panel completely (mean 4 -> 0 -> 0). Checked over 30 s windows with Breathe=1 so the render was animating throughout, so this is not a short-window false inert

feedback: Fix the default first - it is the single most visible gap. The original's untouched render equals its RadiusMode=0.25-0.375 look: three tiny blobs (green 2x2 at ~5 px radius, blue ~5 px, red ~4 px) on a nearly black panel, mean brightness 4. The port boots into its RadiusMode=0.875-1 look (full wedges reaching the panel edge, mean brightness 21). Move the port's RadiusMode default down into its second quarter AND make that quarter draw the original's compact blobs.

Rework RadiusMode modes 0, 1 and 2. Only mode 3 (full-length wedges) matches - it is pixel-exact (mean abs diff 1.0/255), so keep it. Target for the others, on a 16x16 grid with the harness clock: mode 0 = a green wedge running from centre to the left edge plus a small blue cluster, with the red/second hand NOT drawn at all; mode 1 = three compact blobs of 4-5 px each sitting at different radii (green ~5 px out, blue reaching in to the centre, red ~7 px out); mode 2 = the same three features grown to roughly 10-13 px each but still stopping short of the panel edge. The port currently draws isolated single-pixel speckle in modes 0-1 and centre-hugging 3-5 px blobs in mode 2 - it is dropping the radial extent instead of scaling it.

Invert the Speed slider. The original is frozen at Speed=0 and breathes at 1 Hz at Speed=1; the port is the exact mirror (1 Hz at 0, frozen at 1). The waveform and period are already right, so this is a sign flip / 1-minus on the dial mapping only.

Halve the Breathe amplitude. At Breathe=1 and matching Speed, the original's mean brightness swings 18-28 (about +56% over its floor); the port swings 19-37 (about +95%). The 1 s period and waveform shape are already exact - only the depth of the pulse is roughly 1.8x too deep.

Wire up Distance. On the original it visibly scatters/thins the hands in the low RadiusMode modes (at its default mode, mean brightness 4 -> 3 -> 2 across 0/0.5/1) and is deliberately inert in the two high modes. On the port it is inert in the default and low modes and instead blanks the whole panel to black in mode 2 - so its mode gating is off by roughly two modes and its magnitude is far too strong where it does bite.

Sharpness is directionally right but the port's hands stay 25-55% wider than the original's for the same setting (at RadiusMode=1, orig 85/47/25/16/14 vs port 85/53/32/25/20 mean brightness across 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1). Tighten the falloff slightly so the two curves overlay.

Match the control surface: the original exposes three rgbPicker controls named rgbPickerHourHandColor / rgbPickerMinuteHandColor / rgbPickerSecondHandColor. The port exposes hsvPicker controls named hsvPicker*. The rendered colours are equivalent when driven with explicit components, but the widget kind and the control names should follow the original.
